reading:
The judges love this line for its voice and its one round tube. Style ranked the parent first in round 13 (8.2), and in 14a the line got 7 promise votes and the round's biggest gain (+1.02, 7.34). They keep naming the same things to keep: the poster head (a big name beside a square of section ink), one round phosphor tube per page holding the live figure the page does not print (LATE 3, NEXT IN 2 DAYS, SPENT TODAY), the scanlined, haloed lit word, the leadered readout strip of figures that are links (system and skeptic called it the best head device in the heat), the four-shape legend, To do's 'Tick when done' rows with a lit NOW (usability's model), the 01/02/03 folios and the ringed day numerals.

Two things sank it, and every lens said so. First, the colour drained to 88% green (hue entropy .23). All eight lenses asked for the section inks back, at grounded chroma and with a job. Second, the Home radar's waypoint rings sit on bearings that mean nothing. The lessons record this as 14a failed reach 1, a figure that looks like data but is not.

Smaller faults, each named by several lenses:
- Lowercase page names clash with the sentence-case nav (system, type, usability, skeptic).
- Row titles are underlined at rest (soul, skeptic).
- Amber triangles are scattered across the page (skeptic).
- The wordmark is hidden on the phone (feedback, soul, type, usability), and on the phone the tube falls below the first screen.
- Ideas starts below a bare tube and strip.
- Plans has 6 small targets.
- Two kind colours sit only ΔE 8.6 apart.
- 'tell Vera, she'll plan.' sounds as if Vera acts alone, and it was the only lowercase title in the field.

To win, the line should keep the poster and the tube and make the tube tell the truth. The angle on Home's dial should mean days. The lit arc should run from now to next only, which is Trued's and Waypoint's credited light, now on a round tube. Status's tube should become a real meter (Trued's square-root needle), and Plans' tube a calendar leaf. That way each page's circle draws its own data in its own shape and the tubes stop repeating as badges. Colour should come back where it has a job: ink squares, column caps, strip labels, and starters that say where a message usually lands (Departures). The rest stays matte graphite, and the phosphor light comes back only on the circles and the lit word.

briefs.name: Dessau, Dialled
briefs.hypothesis: The carried design rose 1.02 on its strip, its NOW line and its To do. It lost on two counts: 88% green, and a radar whose angle meant nothing. Both are fixable without touching the line's identity. Make Home's round tube a true 28-day dial: the angle is days out, a hand stands at now with the sweep's afterglow trailing behind it, and one arc of the rim is lit from now to the next plan only. The line's signature circle then becomes the tournament's most honest lit figure, and the candidate principle 'light is wired to what it reports' is drawn inside the tube rather than as yet another rail or stem (the field's convergence risk). Give every other page's circle its own shape of data as well: Trued's square-root needle on Status, a torn calendar leaf on Plans, LATE on To do, a numbered map beside the list on Ideas. The 'poster plus badge' repetition style complained of then becomes a system: one round window per page, drawing that page's data. Restore the grounded inks where they carry a job (head squares, column caps, strip labels, starters that say 'usually Plans', kinds pushed apart). That answers the most-cited fix of every lens and brings the green share to about 55-60%. Sentence-case names, underlines at hover only, triangles only where something is late, and the phone fixes clear the remaining marks from usability and the skeptic, without spending the bold poster scale style and type rewarded.
briefs.brief:
Start from x14a-dessau-cross: palettes/x14a-dessau-cross.json, variants/x14a-dessau-cross/sheet.css and templates/*.html, all in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/cross/x14b-a/. Keep its structure on every page: the poster head (name plus a square of section ink, lede, one green primary), the round tube at the head's right, the leadered readout strip of linked figures, the one-line rows, To do's NOW line, the 01/02/03 folios, and the footer's four-shape legend (circle light, square the family's, bar the page, triangle needs a look).

TYPE SYSTEM (write it as tokens at the top of sheet.css). Outfit is display only; the body face stays as now; mono only for figures in fixed columns and on the glass.
- --t-poster: clamp(3.5rem, 6.4vw, 5.5rem) (88px at 1280), Outfit 700, letter-spacing -0.035em, line-height .92. Home's title only.
- --t-page: 4rem (64px), Outfit 650, -0.03em, line-height 1. Every inner page's name, in SENTENCE CASE: 'Things to do', 'Plans', 'Ideas', 'Status', 'Settings', 'Vera', 'Family', 'Memory', 'Wishes'. The words() lowercase heuristic is removed.
- --t-head: 1.875rem (30px), Outfit 600, -0.015em. Section heads: Coming up, To do, Lately added, month name.
- --t-row: 1.125rem/600 for row titles.
- --t-body: 1rem/1.55, with ledes and help capped at max-width: 62ch.
- --t-label: .8125rem caps, tracking .08em. Strip labels and column heads.
- --t-small: .75rem floor.
- Strip figures stay Outfit 300, tabular-nums, 2rem.

THE TITLE. Home's poster reads on two lines, 'Tell Vera.' over 'Let’s plan.' (true curly apostrophe U+2019). It is bone #e6e0d4 at about 88% (color-mix with --bg 12%) so the cream is not the brightest mass. 'plan.', full stop included, is the one lit run: phosphor #6dff9c with the kit's two-layer halo (text-shadow 0 0 2px, 0 0 14px at 55%, 0 0 38px at 25%), and a 1-in-3 scanline raster clipped to the glyphs (background-clip:text over a repeating-linear-gradient), as the carried 'plan.' already does. The box sits directly under it and must stay in the first screen at 1280x900.

HOME'S TUBE: A TRUE 28-DAY DIAL (replaces the half radar with seated rings in home.html, lines ~40-70, and the radar() macro call). Keep the circle (about 22rem), its pewter bezel ring, the power lamp at its foot, the bloom (box-shadow 0 0 60px -10px phosphor at 35%), and the scanline raster on the glass.
- 12 o'clock is NOW, and clockwise angle is days out, 360° = 28 days. The template computes each plan's angle as days_out/28*360; the view already gives relative days, or derive them from the chip date against today.
- Week ticks sit on the rim at 90°/180°/270°, labelled 1w 2w 3w in VT323 14px at 60% phosphor.
- Each coming plan is a 2.75rem waypoint ring ON the rim at its true angle, carrying its day numeral (4, 9, 17, 24). These are the same numerals that lead Coming up's rows. Each ring is an <a> to that row's anchor (#plan-<id>), 44px.
- A NOW hand runs from the hub to 12 o'clock as a bright 2px phosphor line. Behind it (anticlockwise) a 40° conic-gradient afterglow wedge fades from 22% to 0: the sweep's persistence, now meaning 'the hours just past'.
- One arc of the rim is lit, from 12 o'clock to the next ring only. It is an SVG <path> stroke 3px #6dff9c with a filter halo (0 0 6px, 0 0 16px at 40%). The remaining rim from next to the last plan is a 1px dashed pewter (#5d6469) run. Nothing else on the dial glows.
- The hub (inner circle, radius ≤ 62%) holds the words, centred in VT323:
  - 'NEXT UP' (13px caps, 70%)
  - the plan's name at 22px, max two lines, max-width 13rem, text-wrap: balance
  - 'Sun 13:00 · in 2 days'
  - a link '3 more this month →' to #coming, underlined only on hover and focus.
- Under the tube, a 60-80px soft green pool spills onto the ground (radial-gradient, 8% phosphor, no edge).
- With no plans: the dial shows only the NOW hand and the hub says 'Nothing on the dial yet.'

HOME BELOW. The strip stays.
- Strip labels take their section ink: PLANS steel-cyan --plans #86b4ba, TO DO denim --todo #90a8cc, IDEAS heather --ideas #a597b4, TODAY bone, LATE amber with its triangle, which is the only triangle in the strip.
- Strip figures go in wheat #d9c79a; LATE's figure stays amber.
- The setup band loses its amber left bar and triangle. It becomes a steel left bar 3px #7f93a3 with three 2.75rem numbered square steps (squares are the family's), and 'Choose your own password' as the one link.
- Column caps over Coming up, To do and Lately added go back to 4px solid section ink at 75%, with the head's square at full ink.
- Coming up rows lead with the ringed day numeral (1px ring in --plans; the next one's ring is phosphor, lit). They keep the lit NOW at the top of the column only.
- Lately added keeps the kind square with the kind's icon.
- Kinds pushed apart to ΔE ≥ 12, each with its icon so colour is never alone:
  - activity wheat #cdb27a
  - restaurant clay #c58b6b
  - outing sage #8fc29b
  - trip steel #86a9c9
  - show brick-rose #c4898f (replacing the ash rose that sat beside lilac)
  - day trip pewter-teal #8fb3ad
- Kind words stay caps labels in their ink.

STARTERS AS PRINTED KEYS (graft, Departures). The three ways to start become 2.75rem keys on graphite #1a1c1f with a 1px #2a2d30 edge. Each has a 10px SOLID square of the destination's ink at the left (Plans steel-cyan, To do denim, Ideas heather), the words in --ink-2, and at the right a hint in --label with the section's icon: 'usually Plans', 'usually To do', 'usually Ideas'. Hover adds a 2px inset left edge in that ink and lifts the ground 8%. No green on them at rest. Gap .5rem.

LINKS AND MARKS EVERYWHERE.
- Row titles, strip labels and head links carry no underline at rest. On :hover and :focus-visible a 2px underline appears in the row's section ink (text-underline-offset .25em). Prose links in help text keep a 1px underline.
- The amber triangle appears only on the LATE strip cell, on late rows (To do, Home's To do column), and in the footer legend. Settings' 'Sign-in and security' becomes a steel square with 'needs a look' in amber words, no triangle.

TO DO. Keep it as built: the 'Tick when done' head, square ticks, Edit buttons, the NOW line, the strip whose figures filter, and the tube 'LATE 3 TASKS' with the 3 in amber phosphor (#ffc46b with halo) on the glass. Ticks get a 44px hit area around the 1.15rem square well, drawn with a ::before square (no round radius).

PLANS. The round tube becomes a torn calendar leaf (ledger L187), still round. A matte band across the top 32% of the circle (#2a3036, pewter, not teal) carries the next plan's month 'OCT' in --plans caps. Below it, green-black glass holds the day '4' in VT323 4.5rem with halo, and 'Sun · in 2 days' at 14px. The page name 'Plans' gets a lede so no empty band remains beside it: 'Next: Oaks Park roller rink, Sunday 4 October, 13:00'. The month grid's day rings become 2.75rem links (min-width/height 2.75rem, inline-grid centred). Today stays the solid phosphor disc. Plan chips keep a 2px left edge in the plan's kind ink (not all --plans).

STATUS. The round tube becomes a round moving-coil meter (graft, Trued).
- A 240° arc across the upper glass on a square-root scale from $0 to the day's limit, ticks at $0.25 / $1.00 / $2.00 in VT323 12px. A dashed amber tick marks the limit.
- A ghost needle (1px dashed, 35% phosphor) rests on the average day of the last 30 days.
- The live needle (2px phosphor, hot core) has its hub INSIDE the glass at the circle's centre.
- Beside the tube, in words, at body size: 'Spent today $0.00 · average day $0.04 · 0% of $2.00'.
- The 01/02/03 folios move into a 4.5rem left margin column (Outfit 300, 3rem, --faint), the heads align to the text column, and lamps keep the legend's shapes: lit circle working, steel dot waiting, pewter ring off, dashed ring not set up.

IDEAS. The list sits BESIDE the map: grid 1fr 22rem at ≥1100px. The compass radar is position:sticky (top: bar + 1rem) on the right, and its dots are numbered to the rows' #1-#12 in VT323 13px beside each dot. Each dot is an <a> to its row and keeps its true bearing and drive time. The strip (Ideas 12 · Nearest 18 min NW · Furthest 2 h 45 min W) stays above both. The filter row stays.

SETTINGS, CHAT, FORM, FAMILY, MEMORY, WISHES. Sentence-case poster heads at --t-page with their ink squares (Settings and Status pewter #9aa5ae, Vera phosphor-dim, Family clay, Wishes brick-rose). Settings keeps its leadered rows. Chat keeps Vera's round glyph tube in the head; the family's bubbles get a 2px top cap in clay #bf9d80 on #221f1b ground. The new-idea form gets no tube, but its Kind is a select whose options are prefixed by the kind's word in caps.

PHONE (390).
- The bar shows the FamilyDB wordmark beside the mark.
- Home's poster sets at 3.25rem on two lines. A 5.5rem round mini-tube sits at the title's right, holding the next plan's day numeral '4' and 'in 2 d' in VT323, with the lit arc on its rim. It links to #coming. The full dial follows the strip.
- Inner pages keep the round tube beside the page name at 5rem.
- Every target stays at 44px or more.

TOKENS (palette json):
- surface #15171a, surface-2 #1a1c1f (neutral graphite, keep)
- add --wheat #d9c79a, --clay #c58b6b, --pewter #5d6469, --leaf-band #2a3036
- kinds as above
- STYLE.md and the shape legend note: circle = light and the page's live figure; square = the family's (ticks, kind squares, ink squares, setup steps, starter keys); bar = the page (column caps, strip rules, NOW); triangle = late only.
briefs.borrows:
Its own judges' fixes, most-cited first:
- (1) Bring the section inks back at grounded chroma and name what replaces the green: feedback, soul, style, system, type, interaction and the skeptic, all seven. Done with ink squares, 4px column caps, strip labels in section ink, wheat figures, clay family and the kind spread, aiming at about 55-60% green.
- (2) Give Home's radar real meaning or drop the angle: interaction, usability, and the lessons' failed reach 1. The angle now means days out on a 28-day dial.
- (3) Sentence-case page names at 56-64px: system, type, usability and the skeptic. 64px, with the poster title also in sentence case.
- (4) Underline only on hover and focus: soul and the skeptic.
- (5) Restore the wordmark on the phone: feedback, soul, type and usability.
- (6) Move a small tube up beside the title on the phone: soul and system.
- (7) On Ideas, set the list beside the radar: interaction.
- (8) Vary the inner tube by page, a dial on Status and a calendar leaf on Plans: style.
- (9) Cut the amber triangles to LATE only: the skeptic.
- (10) Split the kind colours further apart and keep their icons: usability and the skeptic.
- (11) Fix Plans' 6 small targets: usability.

From the other camp:
- (a) Trued, Headlamp's square-root spend meter, with the ghost needle on the average day, the dashed limit tick and the hub inside the glass. Rebuilt as Dessau's round Status tube, a circle and not Trued's rectangle, with the words beside it in Dessau's body type.
- (b) The lit run from now to the next stop only: Trued, Headlamp's rail (interaction and skeptic: 'the run lit from now to next only') and Waypoint, Ruled's hops, where the Next stop is lit and its arc from Now is lit while the later arcs stay pewter. Waypoint source: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/cross/x14b-b/variants/x14a-waypoint-cross/templates/home.html (lines ~180-195, ol.hops / .hop.is-next) and sheet.css (.hop* rules). Rebuilt as an arc lit on the rim of Dessau's round dial, from the NOW hand to the next waypoint ring, so it lives inside the line's own circle rather than as a rail.

Feedback, style, the skeptic and interaction called them the heat's best grounded colour with a job and best comprehension aid. From the ledger:
- (d) L187, the tear-off calendar leaf (r5-rand-6 Smoke and Lichen; /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/rounds/r5/palettes/r5-rand-6.json). Its caveat is applied: a pewter band #2a3036 instead of teal, kept matte. It is laid across the top of Plans' round tube, so Plans' circle is a leaf.

briefs.avoids:
- 88% green (hue entropy .23) and 'grounded colour gone': feedback, soul, style, system, type, interaction and the skeptic. Inks return with jobs and every removed hue is named and replaced.
- 'The radar's angles mean nothing' and 'a figure that looks like data but is not': interaction, usability, and the lessons' 14a failed reach 1. The dial's angle is days out, and its rings are links to their rows.
- 'Lowercase page names fight the nav': system, type, usability and the skeptic, plus the round-13 note that lowercase beside 'Vera' reads as a typo.
- 'Every row title is underlined, so the page shimmers': soul and the skeptic.
- 'Amber triangles scattered': the skeptic. The setup band is no longer amber either, which also settles the lessons' 'amber with two jobs'.
- 'The wordmark is hidden on the phone' and 'the tube is below the first screen on the phone': feedback, soul, type, usability, and the crossing lessons' phone fault.
- 'On Ideas the list starts below a bare tube and strip': interaction.
- 'The inner pages repeat the same poster-plus-badge layout': style and system. Each circle now draws its own page's data in its own form: a meter, a leaf, LATE, a numbered map.
- 'Kinds only ΔE 8.6 apart, 4.3 for deuteranopes': usability and the skeptic.
- 'Plans' 6 small targets': usability.
- 'The title promises Vera acts alone, and the lowercase is costume': feedback, soul, system and the skeptic.
- The field's convergence: it adds no new rail, stem or footer strip, and takes no ring-as-tick or ring form stops (the lessons' corrected forms), so the round tube stays this line's signature device.
briefs.title: 'Tell Vera. / Let’s *plan.*', set as two poster lines in sentence case, with 'plan.' and its full stop as the one scanlined, haloed lit run. This title is untried. It keeps the line's two-beat poster cadence, which style called the only title with personality, and fixes what the other lenses heard in 'tell Vera, she'll plan.': 'Let's' makes the planning the family's and Vera's together, not a promise that Vera acts alone. The sentence case answers the costume complaint. It still says FamilyDB's job: 'Tell Vera' names who hears the box and invites anything (a weekend, a reminder, an idea, a wish), and 'plan' is the job word, lit last where the eye stops. It differs in words from every title in the field ('Give Vera something to plan.', 'Tell Vera what to plan.', 'What needs a plan?' and the rest), so the judges can weigh it on its own.
